transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’m here because I can’t stop thinking about my hairline and how my face looks under the restaurant lights. I feel like I look old and strange, even though my coworkers tell me they don’t see it.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your appearance in mirrors or other reflective surfaces?

Yes. Before a shift I’ll keep going back to the bathroom mirror, checking my hairline and my face. I take pictures on my phone from different angles, comb my hair forward, then look again. I get stuck thinking about how the guests will see me, and sometimes I’m late or too worked up to go out front.
Are you afraid that other people will judge you because of how you look?
Yes. I feel like people will notice my hairline and how my face looks under those lights and think I look old or strange. My coworkers say they don’t see it, but I can’t really believe them.
Do these thoughts about your hairline and face feel intrusive and hard to control, even when you try to stop thinking about them?

Yes. I try to put it out of my mind, but I keep coming back to my hairline and how my face looks in those restaurant lights. I just feel like I look old and strange, even though people at work tell me they don’t see it.
Do you ever avoid going to work or being seen by other people because of these worries about your appearance?

Yes. I’ve been late or missed shifts because I couldn’t make myself go in, and I’ve been written up at the restaurant for it. I’ve also stopped going to staff photos, gallery events, even hikes sometimes, because I just can’t handle being seen like that.
When you worry about people judging you, is it mainly because of your hairline and face, or do you also feel judged in social situations even when you are not thinking about your appearance?

It’s mainly my appearance. I can’t stop thinking about my hairline and how my face looks under the restaurant lights. I feel like it makes me look old and strange, even when my coworkers say they don’t see it.
Do you think it’s possible that your hairline and face look normal to other people?

I mean, people keep telling me it looks normal, so maybe they really don’t see it. But I can’t believe it when I look in the mirror or see myself under those lights. It still looks old and strange to me.
Do you spend a lot of time trying to hide or fix your hairline or face because of how they look?

Yes. Before a shift I’ll keep checking the bathroom mirror and taking pictures of myself from different angles. I comb my hair forward, try to make it look less obvious, and then I start thinking about how the guests are going to see me. It can go on so long that I’m late, or I get too worked up to go out front.
Are the mirror checking and photo taking mainly to examine or fix how your hairline and face look?

Yes. I’m checking to see how bad it looks and trying to make it less noticeable. I’ll take pictures from different angles, comb my hair forward, then keep thinking about how the guests are going to see me. Sometimes I do it so long before work that I’m late or too upset to go out front.
Aside from worries about your appearance, do you have other unwanted thoughts that lead you to do repeated rituals or checking?
No, I don’t think so. The checking and all that is really about how I look—my hairline and my face.
Are you ever completely convinced that your hairline or face truly looks abnormal to other people?

Yeah, a lot of the time I am. I look at my hairline and then under those restaurant lights my face just looks old and strange to me. My coworkers tell me they don’t see it, but I can’t really believe them—I keep thinking they must notice it too.
